get.summary: Search agreements with matched section previews
get.description: Searches agreements with the same structured filters as `/v1/sections`, including taxonomy IDs and `text_query`, and returns one row per agreement. With `standard_id`, `section_uuid`, or `text_query`, an agreement matches when at least one of its latest sections matches them all; `match_count` counts those sections and `matched_sections` previews the first three in document order (with `text_query`, each snippet is centered on the match and `matched_terms` lists the matched text). `metadata` is rejected: every row already carries the full agreement metadata.
Returns the hierarchical Pandects clause taxonomy: nodes keyed by label, each carrying its `id` (standard ID) and, below L3, its `children`.

Returns, for every clause-taxonomy node, how many sections `GET /v1/sections?standard_id=<id>` matches: a parent node counts the distinct sections tagged with it or any descendant. Nodes with no sections are omitted.
Returns the hierarchical Pandects tax-clause taxonomy tree.

Returns, for every tax-clause-taxonomy node, how many clauses `GET /v1/tax-clauses?tax_standard_id=<id>` matches with default options (rep-and-warranty clauses excluded): a parent node counts the distinct clauses tagged with it or any descendant. Nodes with no clauses are omitted.
Returns NAICS sectors with nested subsectors.
Returns canonical counsel IDs and names for counsel entities referenced across agreements.
Returns newest-first metadata for publicly available database dump artifacts.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only return releases strictly newer than this version (release versions are dump dates, e.g. 2026-07-19; same-day repushes get a numeric suffix such as 2026-07-19.2, which sorts after its base version).

parameters.name: dump_sha256
parameters.description: Only return the release for this dump sha256. Match it against the X-Pandects-Dump-Hash response header (or the dump_version.hash body field) to see exactly which changes the data you are querying includes.

get.description: Returns the changelog for the public database dumps, the REST API, and the MCP surface, newest release first. Each release corresponds to one published bulk dump; match `dump_sha256` against the `X-Pandects-Dump-Hash` response header (or the `dump_version.hash` body field) to see exactly which changes the data you are querying includes. `latest_version`/`latest_released` always describe the newest published release, even when `since`/`dump_sha256` filter the `releases` list.
